info.title: Kokio BFF
info.description:
Backend-for-frontend service for the Kokio platform.

**Responsibilities**
- eSIM catalogue discovery and plan management
- eSIM purchase and topup order orchestration
  (payment session creation → webhook-triggered fulfilment → on-chain recording)
- eSIM management and topup compatibility checking
- Coupon issuance and redemption
- Scheduled job execution (catalogue refresh, secret rotation, order cleanup,
  vendor retry, on-chain retry)

---

## Authentication model

All endpoints except health probes, public catalogue endpoints, and webhook
receivers require authentication. Two protection mechanisms are in use:

### `requireAuth` — DPoP-sender-constrained JWT validation

Protected endpoints require two headers on every request:

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `Authorization` | `DPoP <access_token>` — RS256 JWT issued by the Kokio Auth Server |
| `DPoP` | Fresh DPoP proof JWT per RFC 9449 |

The BFF validates the access token locally via the JWKS cache.
It does **not** call the auth server on the hot path.

The DPoP proof is validated against the `cnf.jkt` claim on the access token,
including `ath` (SHA-256 hash of the access token, base64url-encoded),
`htm`, `htu`, `iat`, and `jti` claims.

After successful validation, `deviceWalletAddress` is extracted from the JWT `sub`
claim and injected as `req.auth.deviceWalletAddress`. This value is used as the
device identity for all downstream operations — **clients must not include
`deviceId` or `deviceWalletAddress` in request bodies or query strings.**

### `requireStepUp` — auth_time recency enforcement

Sensitive endpoints (currently only `POST /order`) additionally enforce
`requireStepUp`, which checks that the `auth_time` claim on the access token
is within a 5-minute recency window (`STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 300`).

If the `auth_time` is stale, the BFF returns `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` (401).
The client must trigger the step-up flow on the Auth Server
(`stepup/begin` → `stepup/complete`) to obtain a fresh access token,
then retry the BFF request.

### `requireAdminToken` — static bearer token

Admin and scheduler endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Two independent token configurations exist:

| Token | Holder | Endpoints |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| `schedulerToken` | Cloudflare cron worker | Catalogue refresh, secrets, jobs, region deny/allow, coupon issuance |
| `internalToken` | Auth Server | Account sync (`POST /admin/accounts/sync`) |

The account sync endpoint additionally enforces an IP allowlist check
**before** token validation.

## DPoP proof requirements

All `requireAuth`-protected endpoints validate the DPoP proof JWT
according to the following rules:

| Claim | Requirement |
|-------|-------------|
| `typ` | Must be `dpop+jwt` |
| `alg` | Must be `ES256` |
| `jwk` | Must be an EC P-256 public key |
| `jti` | UUID v4, single-use — replay is rejected via an in-process TTL store |
| `htm` | Must match the HTTP method of the request |
| `htu` | Must match the HTTP URI of the request (query and fragment stripped) |
| `iat` | Must be within ±60 seconds of server time |
| `ath` | Must be the base64url-encoded SHA-256 hash of the access token presented in the `Authorization` header |

The BFF enforces DPoP key binding via `cnf.jkt` on the access token:
the proof must be signed by the same key pair that was bound at the
original `authorization_code` grant on the Auth Server. A key mismatch
triggers `DPOP_PROOF_KEY_MISMATCH` (401).

DPoP nonce issuance is not currently implemented. The `iat` freshness
window combined with `jti` replay prevention provides adequate protection
at the current stage. Nonce support is tracked as a pre-production
hardening item.

## Correlation ID

All endpoints require the `x-correlation-id` request header, with the
following exemptions:

| Exempt endpoints | Behaviour when header is absent |
|------------------|---------------------------------|
| `GET /health`, `GET /health/ready`, `GET /health/deep` | Server generates a UUID prefixed with `exempt-` |
| `GET /` (root) | Server generates a UUID prefixed with `exempt-` |
| `POST /webhooks/stripe`, `POST /webhooks/moonpay` | Server generates a UUID prefixed with `exempt-` |

On **all other endpoints**, a missing `x-correlation-id` header returns a
`400` response with error code `REQUIRED_HEADER_FIELD` before any further
processing occurs.

The resolved correlation ID is:
- Stored in the per-request `AsyncLocalStorage` context for structured log correlation.
- Echoed in the `x-correlation-id` response header.
- Echoed in the `correlationId` field of every response envelope.

**Idempotency:** On `POST /order`, the `x-correlation-id` value doubles as
the idempotency key. The client must send a consistent unique value per order
attempt and reuse the same value on retries. The order status polling endpoint
`GET /order/{idempotencyKey}` uses this same value as the path parameter.

Clients should generate a UUID v4 per request and use it for client-side
log correlation.

## Rate limiting

Two rate limiters are applied, both backed by `MemoryStore` (single-instance only):

| Limiter | Scope | Window | Max requests | Key |
|---------|-------|--------|--------------|-----|
| Global | All endpoints | 15 minutes | 300 | Client IP |
| Per-device | Authenticated endpoints | 1 minute | 10 | `deviceWalletAddress` (falls back to IP if auth not yet populated) |

The per-device limiter is applied to: `GET /account` `POST /order`, `GET /order/list` `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}`,
`GET /esim`, `GET /esim/{esimId}`, `GET /esim/compatibility/{esimId}`,
`GET /coupon/{code}`.

Rate-limited responses return HTTP `429` with error code `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
Standard `RateLimit-*` headers are included per RFC 6585.

## Admin and webhook endpoints

Admin endpoints (`/admin/*`) are protected by static bearer tokens held only
by internal services and the Cloudflare cron scheduler. Webhook endpoints
(`/webhooks/*`) perform their own HMAC signature verification inside the
handler. Both categories are documented here for backend team reference.
**Client applications cannot and must not call these endpoints.**

## Context path

All paths in this specification are documented without a prefix
(e.g. `/catalogue`, `/order`).

The `/v1` version prefix is applied at runtime via the `CONTEXT_PATH`
environment variable. The deployed path for all endpoints is
`{CONTEXT_PATH}{path}` — currently `/v1/catalogue`, `/v1/order`, etc.
in all environments.

Refer to the environment-specific deployment documentation for the
configured prefix per environment.

tags.name: Account
tags.description:
Authenticated device account endpoints.

`GET /account` returns wallet-derivation material for client-side smart-account
recovery after a reinstall. Requires DPoP-constrained JWT auth and step-up
authentication.

tags.name: Catalogue
tags.description:
eSIM plan discovery endpoints.

`GET /catalogue` and `GET /catalogue/service-regions` are public —
no authentication is required.

`POST /catalogue/refresh` is admin-only and is triggered by the Cloudflare cron worker on a 24-hour schedule.

tags.name: Order
tags.description:
eSIM purchase and topup order orchestration.

**Order initiation** (`POST /order`): Requires `requireAuth` (DPoP-constrained JWT)
and `requireStepUp`. Creates the order and payment sessions. Returns session data
for the client to complete payment via Stripe Payment Elements (FIAT) or
Moonpay hosted page (CRYPTO). Coupon orders with full coverage auto-pay.

**Order status polling** (`GET /order/{idempotencyKey}`): Requires `requireAuth` only.
Poll after payment completion until order reaches a terminal state.

The `deviceId` is injected server-side from the JWT `sub` claim.
Clients must not include it in the request body.

**Pipeline:** order initiation → client-side payment → webhook-triggered fulfilment
→ vendor provisioning → eSIM delivery → on-chain recording.

tags.name: eSIM
tags.description:
eSIM management and topup compatibility checking.

All endpoints require `requireAuth` (DPoP-constrained JWT).
The `deviceId` is injected from the JWT `sub` claim.

`GET /esim` returns all eSIMs for the authenticated device, optionally
filtered to active-only. `GET /esim/{esimId}` returns a single eSIM with
full plan history. Device ownership is enforced on all operations.

`GET /esim/compatibility/{esimId}` checks topup compatibility between
a catalogue plan and the device's active eSIMs.

tags.name: Coupon
tags.description:
Coupon redemption for authenticated devices.

`GET /coupon/{code}` requires `requireAuth`.
`POST /coupon` is admin-only (Cloudflare cron worker token).

tags.name: Health
tags.description:
Liveness, readiness, and deep dependency health probes.

Used by the service hosting platform for deploy health checks and internal monitoring.
Health endpoints do not require authentication or a correlation ID header.

Clients may choose to integrate health services for app status checks and to show
relevant warnings in case of degraded service status.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description:
Internal administration and operational endpoints.

**These endpoints are NOT callable by client applications.**
Documented here for backend team reference.

Includes:
- Secret rotation and status (`/admin/secrets/*`)
- Background job triggers (`/admin/jobs/run`)
- Account synchronisation (`/admin/accounts/sync`)
- Region deny list management (`/admin/regions/deny`)
- Payment processor webhooks (`/webhooks/stripe`, `/webhooks/moonpay`)

Admin endpoints are protected by static bearer tokens validated using
constant-time comparison. Webhook endpoints perform their own signature
verification inside the handler (Stripe HMAC / Moonpay HMAC-SHA256).

get.description:
Returns 200 if the process is running. No dependency checks are performed.

Used by the service hosting platform as a liveness probe to determine
whether the process should be restarted.

Always returns 200 while the process is alive.

200.description: Service process is alive.

get.description:
Returns 200 when the service is ready to handle traffic.

Validates both MongoDB connections (app_data and app_secrets), performs
a required secrets prewarm, and probes the auth server liveness endpoint.

The auth server probe is a soft check. An unreachable auth server is
reported in the response but does not cause a 503. All other checks are
hard and failure returns 503 and removes this instance from rotation.

The service hosting platform uses this probe to gate incoming traffic.

200.description: Service is ready to handle traffic. All hard dependency checks passed.

503.description:
Service is not ready. One or more hard dependency checks failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `APP_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | Application MongoDB is not in a connected state |
| `SECRETS_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | Secrets MongoDB is not in a connected state |
| `PREWARM_FAILED` | Required secrets prewarm failed |

get.description:
Performs a full dependency health check with latency measurements.

Checks both MongoDB connections and their ping latency, required secrets
availability, auth server reachability, and the JWKS cache key count.

**Hard checks** (503 on failure): both DB connections, both DB pings,
required secrets prewarm.

**Soft checks** (always reported, never cause 503): auth server
reachability, JWKS cache key count.

**Caching:** Results are cached for 15 seconds. A cached failure is
re-thrown without re-running checks until the TTL expires. When served
from cache, the response `cached` field is `true` and `latencyMs` is `0`.

This endpoint is used for detailed diagnostics.
`GET /health/ready` should be used for traffic-routing decisions as it is lighter and not cached.

200.description: All hard dependency checks passed.

503.description:
One or more hard dependency checks failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `APP_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | Application MongoDB is not in a connected state |
| `SECRETS_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | Secrets MongoDB is not in a connected state |
| `PING_FAILED` | MongoDB admin ping failed on one or both connections |
| `PREWARM_FAILED` | Required secrets prewarm failed |

A 503 response may itself be served from the 15-second cache if a
previous live check failed within the TTL window.

get.description:
Returns the wallet-derivation material the client SDK needs to reconstruct the
smart account after a reinstall. Identity is resolved server-side from the JWT —
no request body or parameters are accepted.

**Authentication:** Requires DPoP-constrained JWT (`requireAuth`) **and** step-up
authentication (`requireStepUp`). Provide both `Authorization: DPoP` and `DPoP`
headers. Recovery always follows a fresh passkey assertion, so step-up adds no
additional user friction. Step-up recency window is 5 minutes.

**Excluded fields:** `stripeCustomerId` is never returned — it is an internal
billing reference with no client-side use.

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device
limiter (10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

200.description: Account recovery profile for the authenticated device.

401.description:
Authentication, DPoP validation, or step-up recency check failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | Access token missing, malformed, or signature invalid |
| `TOKEN_EXPIRED` | Access token has expired — refresh via Auth Server |
| `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` | Operation requires recent authentication — trigger step-up flow |
| `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` | No account exists for the authenticated device — registration may not have synced |
| `DPOP_PROOF_MISSING` | `DPoP` header is absent |
| `DPOP_PROOF_MALFORMED` | `DPoP` proof structure or header fields are invalid |
| `DPOP_PROOF_SIGNATURE_INVALID` | `DPoP` proof signature verification failed |
| `DPOP_PROOF_BINDING_INVALID` | `DPoP` proof `htm`, `htu`, or `ath` binding mismatch |
| `DPOP_PROOF_STALE` | `DPoP` proof `iat` is outside the ±60-second freshness window |
| `DPOP_PROOF_REPLAYED` | `DPoP` proof `jti` has already been used |
| `DPOP_PROOF_KEY_MISMATCH` | `DPoP` proof key does not match the `cnf.jkt` claim |

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of active eSIM plans for the specified service region.

**Required:** `serviceRegionCode`.
Valid values shall be obtained from `GET /catalogue/service-regions`.

**Pagination:** Results are paginated.
Default page size is `50`, maximum is `250`.
Use `page` and `pageSize` to navigate.

**Plan selection for orders:** Use the `catalogueId` field from a returned
plan as the `catalogueId` parameter in `POST /order`.

**Topup plans:** By default, TOPUP-only plans are excluded from results.
Pass `includeTopup=true` to include them. For topup orders, the server
resolves the correct TOPUP plan automatically from the submitted `catalogueId`
— clients do not need to filter for TOPUP plans specifically.

**Backup plans:** By default, only ACTIVE-status plans (the preferred offering
per equivalence group) are returned. Pass `includeBackup=true` to also
include BACKUP plans.

parameters.name: serviceRegionCode
parameters.description:
Service region code to filter plans by.
Case-insensitive — normalised to uppercase by the server.

Obtain valid values from `GET /catalogue/service-regions`.
Pass the `code` field from any entry in the response.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description:
Filter by vendor identifier.
Case-insensitive — normalised to uppercase.
Omit to return plans from all vendors.

parameters.name: coverageType
parameters.description: Filter by coverage type. Case-insensitive — normalised to uppercase.

parameters.name: includeTopup
parameters.description:
When `true`, includes TOPUP-only plans in results.
When `false` (default), TOPUP-only plans are excluded.

parameters.name: includeBackup
parameters.description:
When `true`, includes BACKUP-status plans alongside ACTIVE plans.
When `false` (default), only ACTIVE-status plans are returned.

BACKUP plans are equivalent offerings outranked by a higher-priority vendor on the compression pass.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Number of results per page.
Defaults to the server-configured default page size.
Subject to a server-configured maximum.

200.description: Catalogue plans returned successfully.

400.description:
Query parameter validation failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `NO_SERVICE_REGIONS_PROVIDED` | `serviceRegionCode` query parameter is missing or empty |
| `INVALID_VALUE` | A parameter value does not match the accepted enum or format |
| `INVALID_PAGINATION_PARAMS` | `page` or `pageSize` is not a valid positive integer or exceeds the maximum |

get.description:
Returns all supported eSIM service regions grouped by coverage type.

Use the `code` field from any returned entry as the `serviceRegionCode`
query parameter on `GET /catalogue`.

Served from in-memory constant maps — no database dependency.

200.description: Service regions returned successfully.

post.description:
Triggers a catalogue refresh from one or more configured eSIM vendors.

Pass `{ "vendors": ["ALL"] }` to refresh all configured vendors,
or a specific list of vendor identifiers for a partial refresh.

**Always returns 200**, the HTTP status reflects successful dispatch,
not per-vendor success.
Inspect `vendorRefreshResults` in the response for per-vendor outcomes.

**Concurrency:** Per-vendor distributed locks prevent overlapping refresh cycles.
A vendor already being refreshed returns `success: false` with a lock contention reason,
this is NOT an error.

**Compression:** The catalogue compression pass runs automatically after
all refreshes settle (if at least one succeeded), reassigning ACTIVE/BACKUP
plan status across equivalent offerings from different vendors.

**Access control:** Requires scheduler admin bearer token.

200.description: Refresh dispatched. Inspect `vendorRefreshResults` for per-vendor outcomes.

vendorRefreshResults.failureReason: Refresh already in progress for VENDOR2

400.description:
Request body validation failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `NO_VENDORS_PROVIDED` | `vendors` array is missing or empty |
| `INVALID_VENDORS` | One or more vendor identifiers are not recognised |

post.description:
Initiates a new eSIM purchase or topup order (Phase 1).

Creates the order, sets up payment sessions with Stripe (and Moonpay for crypto),
and returns the session data the client needs to complete payment.
This endpoint is synchronous from the client's perspective — it returns once the
payment session is ready.

**Fulfilment (Phase 2) is asynchronous.** After the client completes payment
(via Stripe Payment Elements or Moonpay hosted page), the payment provider
sends a webhook to the BFF which triggers vendor fulfilment, eSIM provisioning,
and on-chain recording. Poll `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}` for order status.

**Authentication:** Requires DPoP-constrained JWT (`requireAuth`) and
step-up authentication (`requireStepUp`). Provide both `Authorization: DPoP`
and `DPoP` headers. Step-up recency window is 5 minutes.

**`deviceId` injection:** The authenticated device address is injected
from the JWT — do not include `deviceId` in the request body.

**Idempotency:** The `x-correlation-id` header value is used as the idempotency
key. If an order already exists for the same correlation ID and device, the
existing `{ orderId }` is returned without re-entering the pipeline.
Send a consistent, unique value per order attempt and reuse the same value on retries.

**New eSIM purchase** (`isNewESim: true`): A new eSIM wallet is deployed on-chain
during fulfilment. eSIM installation details are available via the polling endpoint
once the order reaches a completed state.

**Topup order** (`isNewESim: false`): An existing eSIM identified by `esimId` is topped up.
Check compatibility first via `GET /esim/compatibility/{esimId}`.

**Payment method resolution:**
- `coupon` provided and balance covers full amount → `COUPON` (Stripe $0 invoice, auto-pays)
- `isCryptoPayment: true` (no coupon) → `CRYPTO` (Stripe invoice + Moonpay charge session)
- `isCryptoPayment: false` (no coupon) → `FIAT` (Stripe invoice with Payment Elements)

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device limiter
(10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

201.description:
Order initiated. Payment session data returned.

The response shape varies by resolved payment method:
- **FIAT:** `orderId`, `stripeInvoiceId`, `clientSecret` — render Stripe Payment Elements.
- **CRYPTO:** `orderId`, `moonpayChargeId`, `moonpayPaymentPageUrl` — open Moonpay hosted page.
- **COUPON:** `orderId` only — $0 invoice auto-pays, webhook fires immediately. Begin polling.

After payment completion, poll `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}` for fulfilment status.

get.description:
Returns a paginated, most-recent-first list of the authenticated device's
terminal orders. Supports app-local-state recovery after a reinstall.

Distinct from `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}` (single-order status poll): this
endpoint surfaces the device's historical orders as a uniform list. Each item
carries `idempotencyKey` so the client can deep-link back to the single-order
status endpoint for full details.

`installationDetails` are intentionally not provided in the response.
Active eSIMs for a device can be obtained via the `/esim` endpoint which provides
detailed history and installation details of each esim . Only active esims need this
information, hence, the intended method of surfacing this information to the user is
cia the `/esim` endpoint.

**Authentication:** Requires DPoP-constrained JWT (`requireAuth`).
Step-up is **not** required — this is a read-only history endpoint.

**Scope:** Results are restricted to the authenticated device via the JWT
`deviceWalletAddress`. Orders for other devices are never returned.

**Included states:** Only terminal orders are returned —
`COMPLETED`, `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`, `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `VENDOR_FAILED`,
`ESIM_PROVISION_FAILED`, `ON_CHAIN_FAILED`. Abandoned and in-progress orders are
excluded. `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN` is included because the eSIM is
delivered and usable; on-chain recording is deferred to a background job.

**Ordering:** Sorted by `createdAt` descending (most recent first).

**Pagination:** `page` is 1-based (default 1). `pageSize` defaults to 10,
maximum 25. An out-of-range `page` returns an empty `orders` array with the
true `total`. An empty history returns `orders: []` with HTTP 200, not a 404.

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device
limiter (10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Number of results per page. Defaults to 10, maximum 25.
Values above the maximum are rejected with `INVALID_PAGINATION_PARAMS`
(the server does not silently clamp).

200.description: Paginated order history for the authenticated device.

400.description:
Pagination parameter validation failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `INVALID_PAGINATION_PARAMS` | `page` or `pageSize` is not a positive integer, or `pageSize` exceeds the maximum of 25 |

get.description:
Returns the current order state for the given idempotency key,
scoped to the authenticated device.

**Authentication:** Requires DPoP-constrained JWT (`requireAuth`).
Step-up is **not** required — this is a read-only polling endpoint.

**Polling guidance:**
- After completing payment (Stripe Payment Elements or Moonpay hosted page),
  poll this endpoint at a reasonable interval (e.g. every 2–3 seconds).
- Stop polling when `orderStatus` reaches a terminal state.
- Terminal success: `COMPLETED`, `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN` (eSIM is usable).
- Terminal failures: `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `VENDOR_FAILED`, `ESIM_PROVISION_FAILED`,
  `ON_CHAIN_FAILED`, `ABANDONED`.
- For `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`, the eSIM is delivered and functional —
  on-chain recording is deferred to a background job and does not block usage.

**Response shape varies by state.** See the `OrderStatusResponse` schema
for the conditional field presence rules.

**No order found:** If no order exists for the given idempotency key and device,
the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the standard success envelope but all `data`
fields set to `null` (`orderId`, `planId`, `orderStatus`, `paymentMethod`).
The response message will contain `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`. This is not an error —
the client should interpret it as "no order was created with this correlation ID."

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device limiter
(10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

parameters.name: idempotencyKey
parameters.description:
The `x-correlation-id` value used when the order was created
via `POST /order`. This is the idempotency key that uniquely
identifies the order for the authenticated device.

200.description:
Order status returned. The response shape varies by the current `orderStatus`.
See the schema documentation for conditional field presence.

postPaymentFailure.summary: Post-payment failure — flagged for manual review

get.description:
Returns all eSIMs associated with the authenticated device.

**Authentication:** Requires DPoP-constrained JWT (`requireAuth`).

**Filtering:** Pass `activeOnly=true` to return only eSIMs with
`activationStatus: ACTIVE`. When omitted or any other value,
all eSIMs for the device are returned regardless of activation state.

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device limiter
(10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

if the plan is SIM-type, the server finds the TOPUP equivalent automatically.

**Before ordering:** Call this endpoint before submitting a topup order via `POST /order`
to confirm compatibility and identify which `esimId` to use.

**Rate limiting:** Subject to both the global IP limiter and the per-device
limiter (10 requests per minute per `deviceWalletAddress`).

Triggers a single execution of a named background job.

This is the single entry point for all BFF scheduled operations.
The Cloudflare cron worker calls this endpoint on configured schedules for each job.

**Concurrency:** Each job holds a distributed lock for the duration of its execution.
A call while the lock is held is a no-op and returns 200 with `executed: false`.
This is expected behaviour when the cron worker fires before a previous run has completed.

**Always returns 200** — the HTTP status reflects successful dispatch, not job completion.
Inspect `executed` and `result` in the response for the actual outcome.

**Access control:** Requires scheduler admin bearer token.
Not accessible to client applications.

**Available jobs:**

| Job | Window | Description |
|-----|--------|-------------|
| `refresh_vendor1_bearer` | 12 hours | Rotates Vendor1 bearer token |
| `refresh_catalogue` | 24 hours | Refreshes eSIM plan catalogue from all vendors |
| `cleanup_abandoned_orders` | 24 hours | Voids Stripe invoices and marks stuck orders as `ABANDONED` |
| `retry_vendor_fulfilment` | 3 minutes | Retries transient vendor failures (`VENDOR_RETRY_PENDING`) |
| `retry_onchain_recording` | 15 minutes | Retries on-chain recording (`ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`) |

Upserts the BFF Account document from a sync payload pushed by the Auth Server
after a successful passkey registration ceremony.

> Kokio Auth Server. It is documented here for backend team reference.

**Access control:** IP allowlist check (configured via `INTERNAL_ALLOWLIST` env var)
followed by `requireAdminToken(internalToken)`. The IP check runs first — requests
from non-allowlisted IPs are rejected before token validation.

**New accounts:** A Stripe customer is created before the Account document is persisted.
If Stripe customer creation fails, the sync fails entirely (no partial account state).

**Re-registration:** If an Account already exists for the `deviceWalletAddress`,
all credential fields are overwritten with the incoming values. The existing
`stripeCustomerId` is preserved. This handles both same-device re-registration
(passkey deleted and re-created) and cross-device passkey sync (iCloud Keychain,
Google Password Manager).

**Fire-and-forget on the Auth Server side.** The Auth Server calls this endpoint
without awaiting the response. Registration is not affected by sync failures.
Failed syncs can be retried via a manual call.

post.description:
Receives Stripe webhook events for payment confirmation.

> **Not callable by clients.** This endpoint is called exclusively by Stripe's
> webhook delivery infrastructure. It is documented here for backend team reference.

**Authentication:** No auth middleware. Stripe HMAC signature verification is
performed inside the handler using `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` with the
configured webhook signing secret.

**Raw body requirement:** The request body must be the raw unparsed buffer.
The BFF preserves raw bodies for paths starting with `/webhooks` via a
`verify` callback on `express.json()`.

**Handled event types:**
- `invoice.paid` — primary payment confirmation trigger.
- `invoice.overpaid` — treated identically to `invoice.paid`.

All other event types are ignored (200 returned without processing).

**FIAT / Coupon orders:** Validates `invoice.amount_paid` against
`order.amount` (in cents). Performs atomic `PAYMENT_PENDING → PAYMENT_VERIFIED`
transition. Triggers asynchronous fulfilment pipeline.

**Crypto orders** (detected by `moonpayChargeId` presence on the order):
Sets `stripeInvoiceConfirmed = true` and runs dual-confirmation check.
If Moonpay has also confirmed, advances and triggers fulfilment.
Otherwise no-op — the Moonpay webhook completes the dual confirmation.

**Error handling:** All non-signature errors are caught, logged, and return
200 to prevent Stripe retry storms. Only signature verification failures
return a non-200 status.

**Correlation ID:** This endpoint is exempt from the `x-correlation-id`
requirement. A server-generated UUID prefixed with `exempt-` is used.

post.description:
Receives Moonpay webhook events for crypto payment confirmation.

> **Not callable by clients.** This endpoint is called exclusively by Moonpay's
> webhook delivery infrastructure. It is documented here for backend team reference.

**Authentication:** No auth middleware. Moonpay HMAC-SHA256 signature verification
is performed inside the handler. The raw request body is hashed with the configured
Moonpay webhook secret and compared against the `x-signature` header using
constant-time equality.

**Raw body requirement:** The request body must be the raw unparsed buffer.
The BFF preserves raw bodies for paths starting with `/webhooks` via a
`verify` callback on `express.json()`.

**Flow:**
1. Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature of the webhook request.
2. Extract `orderID` from `transactionObject.meta.customerDetails.additionalJSON`
   (the correlation key embedded at charge session creation).
3. Locate the order by `orderID`.
4. Hot-path Stripe invoice status check via `stripe.invoices.retrieve`.
5. If Stripe invoice is paid: set both `moonpayConfirmed` and
   `stripeInvoiceConfirmed`, run dual-confirmation check, advance and fulfil.
6. If Stripe invoice is NOT paid: set `moonpayConfirmed` only, flag order
   for manual review with `HELIO_STRIPE_DISCREPANCY` reason, proceed to
   fulfilment regardless (customer has paid per Moonpay).

**Error handling:** All non-signature errors are caught, logged, and return
200 to prevent Moonpay retry storms. Only signature verification failures
return a non-200 status.

**Correlation ID:** This endpoint is exempt from the `x-correlation-id`
requirement. A server-generated UUID prefixed with `exempt-` is used.

Content-Type is `application/json` but the body is consumed as a raw buffer.

from the nested `transactionObject.meta.customerDetails.additionalJSON`
field which was set during charge session creation.

| `MOONPAY_WEBHOOK_INVALID` | `x-signature` header is absent or HMAC-SHA256 mismatch |

dpopAuth.description:
DPoP-sender-constrained JWT access token.

Two headers are required on every call:

**1. Authorization header**
`Authorization: DPoP <access_token>`

RS-256-signed JWT issued by Kokio Auth Service
(obtained via `POST /auth/token` endpoint).

**2. DPoP Proof Header**
`DPoP: <proof>`

Fresh proof JWT per RFC 9449. See the `DPoP` parameter definition
on each protected operation for the required proof structure.

A new proof must be generated for every request as proofs are single-use
(`jti` replay prevention) and expire after ±60 seconds (`iat` freshness).

DPoP proof validation includes:
   - ath  : SHA-256 hash of the raw access token (base64url), per RFC 9449 §4.3
   - cnf.jkt : JWK thumbprint key binding
   - jti  : replay prevention via in-process TTL store
   - iat  : ±60-second freshness window
   - htm  : HTTP method binding
   - htu  : HTTP URI binding (query and fragment stripped)

**Error handling**

| Code | Status | Trigger |
|------|--------|---------|
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Token missing, malformed, or signature invalid |
| `TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | Access token `exp` has passed — refresh via Auth Server |
| `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` | 401 | Operation requires recent authentication — trigger step-up flow |
| `DPOP_PROOF_MISSING` | 401 | `DPoP` header absent |
| `DPOP_PROOF_MALFORMED` | 401 | Proof structure invalid |
| `DPOP_PROOF_SIGNATURE_INVALID` | 401 | Proof signature verification failed |
| `DPOP_PROOF_BINDING_INVALID` | 401 | `htm`, `htu`, or `ath` mismatch |
| `DPOP_PROOF_STALE` | 401 | `iat` outside ±60-second window |
| `DPOP_PROOF_REPLAYED` | 401 | `jti` already seen |
| `DPOP_PROOF_KEY_MISMATCH` | 401 | Proof key does not match `cnf.jkt` on access token |

bearerAuth.description:
Static admin bearer token.

Required on all endpoints tagged **Admin**. Pass as:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Two independent tokens exist:
- **Scheduler token** — held by the Cloudflare cron worker.
  Required on catalogue refresh, secret rotation, secret status, and job run endpoints.
- **Internal admin token** — held by the Auth Server sync service.
  Required on the internal account sync endpoint (not documented in this spec).

Both are validated using constant-time comparison.
Neither token is accessible to or issued to client applications.

CorrelationId.name: x-correlation-id
CorrelationId.description:
Client-generated request correlation identifier.

Propagated through all log entries produced during the handling of an individual request.
Echoed back in the `correlationId` field of the response envelope.

Use a UUID v4 per request.

DPoP.name: DPoP
DPoP.description:
DPoP proof JWT per RFC 9449.

A compact serialised JWT with:

**Header**
- `typ`: `dpop+jwt`
- `alg`: `ES256`
- `jwk`: client's P-256 public key in JWK format (MUST not contain private key material)

**Payload**
- `jti`: unique proof identifier (UUID v4) — single-use, replay prevented
- `htm`: HTTP method of this request (e.g. `POST`, `GET`) — case-insensitive match
- `htu`: full request URI without query string or fragment
- `iat`: Unix timestamp (seconds) — must be within ±60 seconds of server time
- `ath`: `BASE64URL(SHA256(<raw access token bytes>))` — binds the proof to the specific token

**Signed** with the client's ES256/P-256 DPoP private key.

Generate a fresh proof for every request as the `jti` and `ath` claims
make each proof request-specific and non-reusable.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|------|--------|---------|
| `APP_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Application MongoDB connection is not connected |
| `SECRETS_DB_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Secrets MongoDB connection is not connected |
| `PREWARM_FAILED` | 503 | Required secrets prewarm failed on readiness check |
| `PING_FAILED` | 503 | MongoDB admin ping command failed |

Do NOT use this field for programmatic error handling, use 'code' instead.

planId.description: Vendor-assigned plan identifier. Opaque string, do not parse.

data.description: Data allowance in GB. `null` when `isUnlimited` is `true`.

sms.description: SMS allowance. `null` when not applicable for this plan type.

voice.description: Voice allowance in minutes. `null` when not applicable for this plan type.

isUnlimited.description: `true` if this is an unlimited data plan.

validity.description: Plan validity in days from activation. `null` for plans without a fixed validity window.

isLongDuration.description:
`true` for plans with validity exceeding the long-duration threshold.
Long-duration plans may have different coverage country sets than their
standard-duration equivalents.

isAutoStart.description:
`true` if the plan activates automatically on first data use.
`false` if the plan activates on a fixed date set at purchase time.

isTopupAvailable.description:
`true` if a topup purchase is available for eSIMs already on this plan.
When `true`, an eSIM on this plan can be used in a topup order
(`isNewESim: false`).

Check compatibility first via `GET /esim/compatibility`.

isKycRequired.description:
`true` if the vendor requires KYC verification for this plan.
All current plans have `isKycRequired: false` — Kokio does not collect PII.

serviceRegionCode.description:
Service region identifier. Pass this value as `serviceRegionCode` to
filter `GET /catalogue` results.

Whether this plan is available for new eSIM purchases, topups, or both.

- `SIM` — new eSIM purchase only. A separate TOPUP plan with the same
  coverage exists for topup operations (resolved transparently by the server).
- `TOPUP` — topup purchase only.
- `SIM_OR_TOPUP` — valid for both new eSIM and topup purchases with

planStatus.description:
Compression-pass status assigned by the catalogue service.

- `ACTIVE` — the preferred offering for its equivalence group. Returned
  by default on `GET /catalogue`.
- `BACKUP` — an equivalent plan outranked by a higher-priority vendor

ISO 3166-1 country codes covered by this plan, enriched with
display names. For LOCAL plans this is a single-element array.

plans.description: Paginated array of active catalogue plan entries for the requested service region and filters.

code.description: Region code used as the `serviceRegionCode` filter value on `GET /catalogue`.

name.description: Human-readable display name of the region.

CDN URL for the flag corresponding to the geographical region.

vendors.description:
Array of vendor identifiers to refresh.

Vendor identifier or the special value `ALL`.

vendor.description: Canonical vendor identifier for this result entry.

`true` if the vendor refresh cycle completed successfully.
`false` if any stage failed (API call, transformation, or DB write)
or if a concurrent refresh lock was already held for this vendor.

failureReason.description:
Human-readable reason string when `success` is `false`.
Null when `success` is `true`.

- Error message from the vendor API call or transformation step.

Per-vendor refresh outcome array. Contains one entry per vendor that
was included in this refresh request.

Inspect `success` on each entry to determine vendor-level outcomes.

catalogueId.description:
MongoDB ObjectId of the catalogue entry for the plan being purchased.
Obtain this from the `catalogueId` field on a `GET /catalogue` result.

For topup orders, any active plan from the catalogue may be submitted —
the server resolves the correct TOPUP equivalent plan automatically if
the submitted plan is a SIM-type plan.

isNewESim.description:
`true` for a new eSIM purchase (a new eSIM wallet is deployed on-chain).

`false` for a topup on an existing eSIM (`esimId` is required).

isCryptoPayment.description:
`true` to pay via Moonpay hosted crypto payment page.

`false` to pay via Stripe Payment Elements (FIAT).

Ignored when a `coupon` code is provided that covers the full order amount —
the payment method is resolved to `COUPON` server-side in that case.

esimId.description:
eSIM wallet address of the existing eSIM to top up.

**Required when `isNewESim` is `false`.**

MUST be an eSIM wallet address associated with the authenticated device.
Ownership is verified server-side against the JWT `sub` claim.

Ignored when `isNewESim` is `true`.

coupon.description:
Optional 8-character alphanumeric coupon code.

When provided and the coupon balance covers the full order amount,
the payment method is resolved to `COUPON`. The resulting Stripe
invoice nets to $0 and auto-pays on finalization — no client-side
payment UI is required.

Insufficient balance is a hard rejection (no partial coverage in this version).

qrcode.description:
eSIM activation code extracted from the Apple installation URL.
Present this to the user in a QR code for manual scanning, or use
`appleInstallationUrl` for the one-tap iOS install flow.

Format: `LPA:1$<smdp-address>$<matching-id>`

appleInstallationUrl.description:
Deep link URL for one-tap eSIM installation on iOS.
Open this URL on the user's iOS device to trigger the system eSIM
installation prompt without requiring manual QR code scanning.

Format: `https://esimsetup.apple.com/esim_qrcode_provisioning?carddata=<activation-code>`

orderId.description:
MongoDB ObjectId of the created order document.

Use the `x-correlation-id` header value (which serves as the idempotency key)
to poll order status via `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}`.

stripeInvoiceId.description:
Stripe invoice ID. Present only on **FIAT** orders.

Not directly needed for Payment Elements rendering — use `clientSecret` instead.
Retained for client-side logging and support reference.

clientSecret.description:
Stripe `confirmation_secret.client_secret` for the finalized invoice.
Present only on **FIAT** orders.

Pass this value to Stripe Payment Elements to render the payment form
and complete the payment client-side.

moonpayChargeId.description:
Moonpay charge session ID. Present only on **CRYPTO** orders.

Used for client-side checkout session URL construction.

moonpayPaymentPageUrl.description:
Moonpay hosted payment page URL. Present only on **CRYPTO** orders.

Open this URL in an in-app browser or WebView to present the
Moonpay crypto payment interface to the user.

orderId.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the order document.

planId.description:
Vendor-assigned plan identifier. For topup orders where the server
resolved a TOPUP equivalent, this reflects the resolved plan ID.

orderStatus.description:
Current pipeline stage of the order.

**In-progress states** — keep polling:
- `CREATED` — order document persisted, payment session not yet created.
- `PAYMENT_PENDING` — payment session returned to client, awaiting payment completion.
- `PAYMENT_VERIFIED` — payment confirmed by processor webhook(s).
- `VENDOR_PROCESSING` — vendor fulfilment API call dispatched.
- `ESIM_PROVISIONED` — vendor confirmed, eSIM record saved.
- `VENDOR_RETRY_PENDING` — vendor call failed with transient error, queued for cron retry.
- `ON_CHAIN_SUBMITTED` — on-chain transaction submitted (legacy path).

**Terminal success** — stop polling, eSIM is usable:
- `COMPLETED` — all stages successful.
- `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN` — eSIM delivered and usable, on-chain recording deferred to background job.

**Terminal failures** — stop polling:
- `PAYMENT_FAILED` — payment not collected, prompt user to retry.
- `VENDOR_FAILED` — payment collected, vendor rejected, flagged for manual review.
- `ESIM_PROVISION_FAILED` — payment collected, eSIM delivery failed, flagged for manual review.
- `ON_CHAIN_FAILED` — payment collected, on-chain recording failed after retry exhaustion, flagged for manual review.
- `ABANDONED` — no payment received within the cleanup TTL.

paymentMethod.description: Payment method resolved at order initiation.

vendor.description:
Canonical vendor identifier that fulfilled the order.
Present only when `orderStatus` is `COMPLETED` or `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`.

isNewESim.description:
Whether this was a new eSIM purchase or a topup.
Present only when `orderStatus` is `COMPLETED` or `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`.

iccid.description:
Integrated Circuit Card Identifier assigned by the vendor.
Present only when `orderStatus` is `COMPLETED` or `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`.

esimId.description:
eSIM wallet contract address on-chain.
Present only when `orderStatus` is `COMPLETED` or `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`
and the eSIM record has been persisted.

installationDetails.description:
eSIM installation data for device activation.
Present only when `orderStatus` is `COMPLETED` or `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`,
`isNewESim` is `true`, and the eSIM record contains installation details.

`null` for topup orders.

stripeInvoiceUrl.description:
Stripe hosted invoice page URL.
Present on `COMPLETED`, `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`, and post-payment
terminal failure states. Provides a payment receipt reference for the user
and for support contact in failure scenarios.

flaggedForManualReview.description:
`true` when the order failed after payment was collected and requires
manual customer support resolution.
Present only on post-payment terminal failures:
`VENDOR_FAILED`, `ESIM_PROVISION_FAILED`, `ON_CHAIN_FAILED`.

manualReviewReason.description:
Structured reason code for the manual review flag.
Present only when `flaggedForManualReview` is `true`.

Values:
- `PLAN_DEACTIVATED` — plan was deactivated between payment and fulfilment.
- `ON_CHAIN_RECORDING_FAILED` — on-chain buyDataBundle recording failed after retry exhaustion.
- `VENDOR_FULFILMENT_FAILED` — vendor API permanently rejected the order.
- `ESIM_DELIVERY_FAILED` — eSIM wallet deployment or record persistence failed.
- `WALLET_REGISTRATION_FAILED` — on-chain device wallet registration failed.

orderId.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the order document.

idempotencyKey.description:
The order's idempotency key (the `x-correlation-id` used at creation).
Use as the path parameter for `GET /order/{idempotencyKey}` to deep-link
to full order detail.

planId.description:
Vendor-assigned plan identifier. For topup orders where the server resolved
a TOPUP equivalent, this reflects the resolved plan ID.

orderStatus.description:
Terminal state of the order. Constrained to the states surfaced by the
history endpoint.

**Terminal success** (eSIM usable):
- `COMPLETED` — all stages successful.
- `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN` — eSIM delivered and usable, on-chain recording deferred.

**Terminal failures:**
- `PAYMENT_FAILED` — payment not collected.
- `VENDOR_FAILED` — payment collected, vendor rejected, flagged for manual review.
- `ESIM_PROVISION_FAILED` — payment collected, eSIM delivery failed, flagged for manual review.
- `ON_CHAIN_FAILED` — payment collected, on-chain recording failed after retry exhaustion, flagged for manual review.

paymentMethod.description: Payment method resolved at order initiation.

Canonical vendor identifier that fulfilled the order.
Null on orders that failed before vendor fulfilment (e.g. `PAYMENT_FAILED`).

isNewESim.description:

Null on orders that failed before fulfilment.

iccid.description: ICCID of the provisioned eSIM. Null on orders that did not reach provisioning.

esimId.description:

Null on orders that did not reach provisioning.

stripeInvoiceUrl.description: Hosted Stripe invoice URL for the order, where available.

Whether the order was flagged for manual review (set on post-payment
fulfilment failures). Defaults to false.

manualReviewReason.description: Reason the order was flagged for manual review. Null when not flagged.

createdAt.description: Order creation timestamp. Used as the descending sort key.

orders.description:
Paginated array of the device's terminal orders, most-recent-first.
Empty array when the device has no terminal orders, or when `page`
is beyond the available range.

pageSize.description: Number of results per page as resolved by the server.

total.description: Total number of matching terminal orders across all pages.

esimId.description:
eSIM wallet address for this result entry.
Use this value as `eSimId` in `POST /order` for a topup order if `compatible` is `true`.

iccid.description: Integrated Circuit Card Identifier (`ICCID`) of the eSIM.

vendor.description: Canonical vendor identifier for the eSIM being checked.

compatible.description:
`true` if the vendor confirmed this eSIM is compatible with the resolved TOPUP plan.

`false` in three cases:
- `vendorMismatch: true` — eSIM vendor does not match the plan vendor
- `checkError: true` — the vendor API call failed for this eSIM
- Vendor returned incompatible — the plan cannot be topped up on this eSIM

vendorMismatch.description:
`true` if the eSIM's vendor does not match the plan's vendor.
Cross-vendor topups are not supported.
This eSIM's check is skipped without calling the vendor API.

When `true`, `compatible` is always `false` and `checkError` is always `false`.

checkError.description:
`true` if the upstream vendor compatibility API call failed for this eSIM.
The failure is caught and recorded here rather than propagating.
Other eSIMs in the same request are unaffected.

When `true`, `compatible` is always `false` and `vendorMismatch` is always `false`.

planId.description:
MongoDB ObjectId of the catalogue entry submitted in the `planId` query parameter.
Reflects the input, not the resolved plan.

resolvedPlanId.description:
Vendor-assigned plan ID used for the upstream compatibility API call.
When `topupPlanResolved` is `true`, this is the ID of the TOPUP
equivalent plan, not the originally submitted plan's vendor ID.

topupPlanResolved.description:
`true` if the submitted `planId` was a SIM-type plan and the server
substituted it with its active TOPUP equivalent for the compatibility check.

When `true`, submit the same original `catalogueId` to `POST /order` with `isNewESim: false`.
The server applies the same TOPUP plan resolution transparently during order creation.

results.description:
Per-eSIM compatibility check results.

Contains one entry per active eSIM checked.
When `esimId` was provided in the request, this array contains exactly one entry.
When omitted, all active eSIMs for the device are checked and one entry per eSIM is returned.

iccid.description:
Integrated Circuit Card Identifier assigned by the vendor.
Canonical identifier for the eSIM at the device/system level.

matchingId.description:
LPA matching identifier used in the eSIM activation QR code.
Part of the SM-DP+ activation code alongside `smdpAddress`.

smdpAddress.description:
SM-DP+ server address used for eSIM profile download.
Combined with `matchingId` to form the LPA activation string.

esimId.description:
Smart contract wallet address of the deployed eSIM wallet on-chain.
Primary lookup key for topup orders. Unique per eSIM.

deviceId.description:
EVM wallet address of the device that owns this eSIM.
Logical foreign key to the Account collection.

vendor.description:
Canonical vendor identifier that provisioned this eSIM.
Used for routing topup compatibility checks and vendor API calls.

planId.description:
Catalogue plan identifier at the time of provisioning.
Used as the basis for equivalence key resolution when finding
a compatible TOPUP plan.

planHistory.description:
Chronological record of all orders (initial purchase and subsequent topups)
applied to this eSIM. The first entry is the initial purchase.

activationStatus.description: Current activation lifecycle state of the eSIM.

installationDetails.description:
eSIM installation data for device activation.
Present on new eSIM purchases that have been provisioned.
May be absent on topup-only eSIMs or if the vendor has not yet
delivered installation details.

eSIMUniqueIdentifier.description:
Deterministic UUID derived from `deviceWalletAddress + iccid` via
`esimUidGenerator.hashStringsToUUID`. Used as the on-chain eSIM
identifier for `buyDataBundle` smart contract calls.

updatedAt.description: Mongoose timestamp — last document update time.

orderId.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the order that triggered this plan activation.

planId.description: Vendor plan identifier at the time of purchase.

validity.description:
Plan validity in days, sourced from the catalogue document at fulfilment time.
The eSIM document is self-contained for plan history display without
cross-collection joins.

purchaseDate.description: Vendor-confirmed purchase date from the vendor fulfilment API response.

eSims.description:
Array of eSIM documents associated with the authenticated device.
Empty array when no eSIMs exist for the device.

When `activeOnly=true` is provided, only eSIMs with
`activationStatus: ACTIVE` are included.

hash.description:
On-chain transaction hash of the vault transfer that triggered coupon issuance.
Unique — one coupon per transaction hash is enforced at both application and database layers.

network.description:
Blockchain network on which the originating transaction was submitted.
MUST be a supported network.

tokenName.description:
Token identifier used in the originating vault transfer.
MUST be a supprted token.

vault.description:
EVM address of the vault that received the originating transfer.
Sourced from server configuration at issuance time.

amount.description: Transfer amount as a string-serialised decimal value in the token's native denomination.

code.description:
8-character alphanumeric coupon code.
Uppercase, excluding visually ambiguous characters (I, O, 0, 1).

Pass this value as the `coupon` field in `POST /order` to apply
the coupon to an order (currently accepted but not yet active).

tokenName.description: Token identifier of the balance held by this coupon.

network.description: Blockchain network of the originating vault transfer transaction.

totalAmount.description:
Original total amount at issuance time, serialised as a decimal string.
Immutable after creation — reflects the amount of the originating transfer.

balance.description:
Current remaining balance, serialised as a decimal string.
Decremented on each successful order redemption.
When balance reaches zero, `isExhausted` is set to `true`.

isExhausted.description:
`true` when the coupon balance has been fully consumed.
An exhausted coupon cannot be applied to further orders.

issuedFromTx.description: Audit record of the on-chain transaction from which this coupon was issued.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of coupon creation.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last modification to this coupon document.

lastRedeemedAt.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent successful balance debit.
`null` if this coupon has not yet been redeemed.

lastRedeemedBy.description:
`deviceWalletAddress` of the device that most recently redeemed this coupon.
`null` if this coupon has not yet been redeemed.

redemptions.description:
Array of redemption reference records from `redemptionRefs` on the Mongoose document.
Each entry records a successful balance debit operation against this coupon.
`null` or empty array if no redemptions have occurred.

amount.description: Amount debited from the coupon balance, as a decimal string.

by.description: `deviceWalletAddress` of the device that performed the redemption.

reference.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the order that consumed this balance.

txnHash.description:
On-chain transaction hash of the vault transfer from which to issue the coupon.

The server verifies this transaction on-chain and creates a coupon
with a balance equal to the verified transfer amount.

Must not have been used to issue a prior coupon — enforced at both
application and database layers (`COUPON_ALREADY_ISSUED_FOR_TX`).

network.description:
Blockchain network on which the transaction was submitted.
MUST be a supported network.

tokenName.description:
Token identifier used in the vault transfer transaction.
MUST be a supported token.

name.description:
Canonical secret name identifying which secret to rotate.

Must be a rotatable secret registered in the BFF secrets configuration.
Non-rotatable and unrecognised names are rejected with `INVALID_VALUE`.

Known rotatable secret names are internal — consult the BFF secrets
configuration (`src/configs/secretsConfig.js`) for the canonical name list.

ok.description:
`true` when the secret record was successfully retrieved and is in a healthy state.
Always `true` on a 200 response.

name.description:
Fully qualified canonical secret name as stored in the app_secrets database.

Naming convention: `<type>.<scope>.<vendor>.<identifier>`

- `rotatable.*` — secrets with a TTL that are rotated on a schedule.
  These carry `expiresAt` and `secondsToExpiry` on the `current` entry
  and a `graceUntil` timestamp on the `previous` entry.
- `static.*` — secrets that do not expire or rotate automatically.
  These have `expiresAt: null`, `secondsToExpiry: null`, and
  `previous: null`.

current.description: The currently active version of this secret.

version.description:
UUID v4 identifying this specific version of the secret.
Changes on every rotation.
Use this to confirm a rotation has taken effect.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this secret version was written to the database.

activeFrom.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this version became the active
current secret.
Slightly earlier than `createdAt`,
reflects the start of the rotation transaction rather than the DB write completion time.

expiresAt.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this secret version expires.

Non-null for `rotatable.*` secrets — the secret is considered stale
after this timestamp and the BFF will reject requests using it.

`null` for `static.*` secrets — no expiry is enforced.

secondsToExpiry.description:
Seconds remaining until this secret version expires, calculated at response time.

Non-null for `rotatable.*` secrets.

`null` for `static.*` secrets.

previous.description:
The previous version of this secret, retained during the grace period
to allow in-flight requests using the old value to complete.

Non-null for `rotatable.*` secrets after at least one rotation.
`null` for `static.*` secrets (no rotation history) and for rotatable
secrets that have never been rotated (only bootstrapped).

version.description: UUID v4 identifying this previous secret version.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this version was written to the database.

activeFrom.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this version was the active current secret.

graceUntil.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp marking the end of the grace period for this previous version.

During the grace period the previous secret version remains valid
alongside the new current version. After this timestamp the previous
version is no longer accepted and can be safely purged.

job.description:
Canonical job name identifying which job to run.

Must be one of the configured job names in `src/configs/jobConfigs.js`.
Unrecognised names are rejected with `INVALID_VALUE`.

| Job name | Window | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `refresh_vendor1_bearer` | 12 hours | Rotates the Vendor1 bearer token via the vendor auth endpoint and persists the new value in the secrets store |
| `refresh_catalogue` | 24 hours | Fetches the latest plan catalogue from all configured vendors, upserts plan documents, and runs the compression pass |
| `cleanup_abandoned_orders` | 24 hours | Voids/deletes Stripe invoices and marks orders stuck in `CREATED` or `PAYMENT_PENDING` beyond the 24-hour TTL as `ABANDONED`. Deletes `ABANDONED` orders older than 30 days |
| `retry_vendor_fulfilment` | 3 minutes | Retries orders at `VENDOR_RETRY_PENDING` (transient vendor failures). Max 2 retries before `VENDOR_FAILED` |
| `retry_onchain_recording` | 15 minutes | Retries `buildBuyDataBundleTxn` for orders at `ESIM_PROVISIONED_PENDING_CHAIN`. Max 2 retries before `COMPLETED` + `flaggedForManualReview` |

RunJobResponse.description:
Job execution result. Shape varies by job type. 
Core fields are documented here. Inspect `result` for job-specific outcome details.

job.description: Canonical name of the job that was invoked.

executed.description:
`true` if the job ran to completion (success or failure).

`false` if the job was skipped — typically due to a distributed lock
collision indicating a concurrent run is already in progress.

result.description:
Job-specific result payload. Shape depends on the job invoked.

- `refresh_catalogue`: contains `vendorRefreshResults` array
  (same shape as `POST /catalogue/refresh` response data).
- `refresh_vendor1_bearer`: minimal acknowledgement object.
- `cleanup_abandoned_orders`: contains count of orders updated.

`null` when `executed` is `false`.

P-256 public key coordinates and salt.

Used as the upsert filter key on the Account collection.

Serves as the stable per-device WebAuthn user handle and as the

pubKeyX.description:

0x-prefixed hex string.

pubKeyY.description:
P-256 Y coordinate from the COSE key extracted during registration verification.
0x-prefixed hex string.

salt.description:

stripeCustomerId.description:
Stripe customer ID created at first sync or preserved from the existing account.
All subsequent Stripe invoices for this device are issued against this customer.

code.description:
Service region code to add to the denylist.
Automatically uppercased server-side.

When a region is denied, its LOCAL plans are excluded from
`GET /catalogue` results and its code is excluded from
`GET /catalogue/service-regions` countries list.

REGIONAL, GLOBAL, and CUSTOM_REGIONAL entries are never affected.
Uppercased service region code that was acted upon.
